Graphic Design News Ideas DKS Turns Apple History Into Participatory Experience

DKS Turns Apple History Into Participatory Experience

iPod Dance lets visitors step inside the visual language of Apple's iconic silhouette campaign rather than simply looking at it. The interactive experience was developed for the Mimms Museum of Technology and Art in Roswell GA.

What if you could step inside one of Apple‘s most iconic ad campaigns?

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:20
Instaread

That was the idea behind iPod Dance, one of the interactive experiences DKSDesign developed for iNSPIRE: 50 Years of Innovation from Apple at the Mimms Museum of Technology and Art in Roswell GA.

iNSPIRE is built around a collection of more than 2,000 Apple artifacts spanning five decades of the company’s history. The challenge with the interactive pieces was figuring out where DKSDesign could help visitors connect with that history in a different way.

Apple’s silhouette campaign was an obvious opportunity.

The focus wasn’t on recreating the campaign. It was on capturing the same energy in a way that works in a live environment.

The user walks into frame and their silhouette appears instantly, larger than life on the wall, with iPod and earbuds attached. A camera captures their movement in real time and reduces them to a high-contrast silhouette. That silhouette is placed onto a bold color background, with white earbuds and a device layered in to match the original visual style. The earbuds wire is elastic and responsive, which adds a physical layer to the interaction.

There’s no onboarding. No instructions. The real-time feedback makes it clear how it works, so the interaction teaches itself.

The system supports multiple participants at once, assigning distinct color environments to each person. This allows for shared interaction without confusion and encourages group participation.

Each session is automatically recorded and turned into a short video that can be accessed on-site. What starts as a quick interaction usually turns into something people repeat or share.
